title: Volumetric Fire Shader with Heat Distortion
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a Three.js scene featuring a volumetric fire shader with heat distortion post-processing. Requirements:

## Scene Setup
- Black background, perspective camera at (0, 2, 5) looking at origin
- A ground plane (dark gray, 10x10) at y=0
- A fire source mesh (cylinder, radius 0.3, height 0.1) at origin on the ground plane
- The fire is rendered as a fullscreen quad with a custom fragment shader using raymarching through a volume
- The fire volume is a vertical column (radius ~0.5, height ~2.5) above the fire source

## Volumetric Fire Shader
- Use raymarching (minimum 32 steps) through a 3D noise field (FBM with 4 octaves)
- Noise is animated over time to simulate rising flames
- Color ramp from dark red (base) -> orange -> yellow -> white (hottest core)
- Temperature field drives both color and density: higher temperature = brighter, less dense (flames thin at top)
- Expose shader uniforms: fireIntensity (0.1-3.0, default 1.0), fireSpeed (0.1-5.0, default 1.5), fireHeight (0.5-4.0, default 2.5), noiseScale (0.5-3.0, default 1.2)

## Heat Distortion Post-Processing
- Render scene to an offscreen framebuffer
- Apply a second pass that distorts UVs based on a heat map derived from the fire's screen-space position
- Distortion strength uniform: distortionStrength (0.0-0.1, default 0.03)
- Distortion uses animated sine waves modulated by distance from fire center
- The distortion should only affect areas above the fire (simulating rising heat)

## User Interactions
- Mouse drag (left button): orbit camera around the fire
- Scroll wheel: zoom in/out (clamp distance 2-12)
- Keyboard 'I'/'K': increase/decrease fireIntensity by 0.2 (clamped)
- Keyboard 'J'/'L': decrease/increase fireSpeed by 0.3 (clamped)
- Keyboard 'U'/'O': increase/decrease fireHeight by 0.3 (clamped)
- Keyboard 'H': toggle heat distortion on/off
- Keyboard 'P': pause/resume animation
- Keyboard 'R': reset all parameters to defaults
- Keyboard 'Z': undo last parameter change (maintain history stack of up to 20 entries)
- Keyboard 'Y': redo parameter change
- A DOM button '#btn-snapshot' that captures current parameter state and stores it in window.__3D_STATE__.snapshot

## HUD/UI
- Top-left overlay showing: fireIntensity, fireSpeed, fireHeight, noiseScale, distortionStrength, FPS, paused state, distortion enabled state
- The HUD updates every frame
- A '#btn-snapshot' button in top-right corner

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose the following on window.__3D_STATE__:
- fireIntensity: current float value
- fireSpeed: current float value
- fireHeight: current float value
- noiseScale: current float value
- distortionStrength: current float value
- distortionEnabled: boolean
- paused: boolean
- elapsedTime: float (shader time in seconds, stops incrementing when paused)
- cameraDistance: float (distance from origin)
- cameraAzimuth: float (horizontal angle in radians)
- rayMarchSteps: integer (current step count, always >= 32)
- frameCount: integer (increments each render frame)
- undoStackSize: integer (number of entries in undo history)
- redoStackSize: integer (number of entries in redo history)
- snapshot: object or null (last captured snapshot with all parameter values)
- lastAction: string (name of last user action performed, e.g. 'increaseIntensity', 'toggleDistortion', 'undo', 'redo', 'reset', 'snapshot')
- colorRampMin: [r,g,b] array (base color of fire, normalized 0-1)
- colorRampMax: [r,g,b] array (hottest color of fire, normalized 0-1)
physics_constraints: Fire temperature field must decrease monotonically with height (hotter at base, cooler at top). Heat distortion magnitude must be proportional to proximity to fire center and only apply above the fire source (y > 0 in screen space relative to fire). All shader uniforms must remain within their defined clamped ranges at all times. Time must not advance when paused. Undo/redo must perfectly restore previous parameter states.
